channel.title: Haas Prep
channel.description:
Plain-English prep for upcoming Berkeley Haas FTMBA lectures. Each episode walks through the assigned material for one class session so you arrive ready to think instead of translate.
Every episode names its sources in the description and in the opening. Episodes are original explanation written by a student, not recordings or readings of any course material. Nothing here reproduces slides, cases, or textbook text.
This is an independent student study project. It is not affiliated with, produced by, or endorsed by the Berkeley Haas School of Business or the University of California.

item.title: Tue Sep 1 · MBA 205 Class 3: Knowing Yourself and Others
item.description:
Meets 9:00am, N300 Chou Hall.
Your Big Five results come back. Myers-Briggs versus the Big Five in a fair fight, why the popular one lands halfway between science and astrology, and why the test that flatters you wins on popularity every time.
Sources used to write this episode: - Personality Tests Aren't All the Same (Scientific American, Feb 2024), study.net pack - MBA 205 Class 3 Canvas page - Obsidian index note
Note: 'Do Not Bring Your Whole Self to Work' (NYT) is paywalled; only the opening was readable, and the episode says so
Note: Assigned exam format video not viewable
Original student study material. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Berkeley Haas.

item.title: Tue Sep 1 · MBA 202 Topic 3: The Income Statement
item.description:
Meets 2:00pm, N470 Chou Hall.
The balance sheet is a photograph, the income statement is the movie. Cash basis versus accrual, the matching principle, why a Starbucks gift card is not revenue, channel stuffing and why it always unwinds, and the two different ways to be a profitable business.
Sources used to write this episode: - Topic 03 Income Statement class notes (Even-Tov), Canvas - Libby 11th ed. ch 3 (bookshelf) - Practice Problem 2 Income Statement (Canvas) - 8/27 Balance Sheet lecture transcript - Obsidian index note
Note: Shelved Libby is 11th ed., course cites 10th; chapters used, page references avoided
Original student study material. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Berkeley Haas.

item.title: Tue Sep 1 · INDENG 240 Lecture 2: A First Linear Programming Example
item.description:
Meets 11:00am, Valley Life Sciences.
A coffee shop with limited milk and espresso. Why making all of the profitable drink strands the other ingredient, how decisions, constraints and an objective turn that into a solvable problem, and why the answer always sits at a corner.
Sources used to write this episode: - Kerger pre-notes, Lecture 2 (handwritten, read via page rendering) - INDENG 240 Day 1 deck - Obsidian index note
Note: Pre-notes are a fill-in-the-blank skeleton; the episode covers the setup and questions, not answers not yet given
Original student study material. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Berkeley Haas.

item.title: Mon Aug 31 · MBA 200S Class 3: Sampling Variation and Sampling Bias
item.description:
Meets Axe 9:00am / Oski 2:00pm, N570 Chou Hall.
Bias moves the center, variation is the spread. Why averaging shrinks uncertainty by the square root of n, why the Central Limit Theorem makes the normal curve unavoidable, and why more data cannot fix a bad sample.
Sources used to write this episode: - Stine & Foster 3e ch 14.1 (bookshelf) - 8/28 GSI discussion transcript - 8/26 Class 2 lecture transcript - Class 3 Canvas page
Note: No assigned reading for this session; ch 14.1 used as the topic-matching chapter, stated in the episode
Note: Slides post morning of class
Original student study material. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Berkeley Haas.

item.title: Mon Aug 31 · MBA 201A Lecture 3: Cost Curves and Supply
item.description:
Meets 2:00pm, N370 Chou Hall.
Produce where price equals marginal cost, know when to shut down, and see how John Deere's cost system made an efficient plant look like the most expensive in the industry.
Sources used to write this episode: - John Deere Component Works (A), HBS 9-187-107 - The High Cost of Low Wages, Cascio HBR 2006 - Walmart tariff price hikes, WSJ May 2025 - MIC 4.6 Average and Marginal Costs (Panopto transcript) - Lecture 3 Canvas page
Note: Lecture 3 slides post shortly before class
Original student study material. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Berkeley Haas.
